extractor_notes: TDG's 10-K is characteristic of a sole-source aftermarket components supplier: it does NOT name specific Pentagon Program Elements (PEs), DoD program titles, or PE numbers. Defense exposure is described as a broad mix (~39% of FY2023 net sales) rather than tied to named programs.

Because the filing avoids named-program claims, the J-Book divergence pattern (named-PE-vs-zeroed-budget) has limited surface area. We extract instead: (a) the broad defense-aftermarket and DoD-budget-dependence claims that are implicitly J-Book-grounded, (b) the macro DoD-budget-trend claim the company makes, (c) one F-35 mention that turned out to be a page artifact (control), and (d) standard non-J-Book control claims (counterparty disclosure, OIG audit posture).

Per entity-resolution and J-Book-entity indexes, TransDigm is NOT a prime contractor in the 410-PE J-Book corpus; the corpus tracks named primes (Lockheed, Northrop, etc.) on RDT&E and select procurement lines. Components-supplier exposure is captured (if at all) via the underlying platform's procurement line in P-40 exhibits.
